chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from some of his companions, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: "A man may alter his will, so he may free a slave whom he had commanded to be owned, and own a slave whom he had commanded to be freed, and give to a person whom he had deprived, and deprive a person whom he had given, as long as he has not died and has returned to it."

key_terms.حَرَم: To deprive or exclude from inheritance/gift
key_terms.عِتْق: Manumission or freeing of a slave

ai.seo_question: Can a person change their will before they die according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him) and cited in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the revocability of the will (*wasiyyah*) prior to death, distinguishing it from the finality of inheritance distribution. It highlights the testator's autonomy to alter dispositions regarding manumission and gifts, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the flexibility of bequests before the estate is finalized.
